risks.title: Gas Export Pressure to NCS2 Pipeline
risks.description:
- The design of discharge pressure of the gas compressor does not meet the current Pipeline requirement from PVGAS.

CPY request to execute DE scope to increase back pressure at the hanger flange of ST-CGF export pipeline to NCS 2 from 115barg to 151barg leading to increase compressor discharge pressure. In order to keep one stage of compressor, the pressure at compressor suction should be increased as well.
risks.cause:
1. Possibly FEED optimization result
2. The current compressor design is based on assumptions which were used in FEED (70-90 barg arrival pressure at Dinh Co GPP), while PVGAS has confirmed that the required inlet pressure at Dinh Co GPP is 100-109 barg due to the booster compressors are no longer operating at Dinh Co terminal, and up to 151 barg during line-packing operations.
- With the current selected compressor, the export pressure at delivery point is designed at 115 barg in normal operation. With available power margin, the compressor can achieve higher discharge pressure and meet 123 barg at delivery point, which is significantly lower than the NCS2 pipeline normal operating pressure (estimated as about 130barg at ST-CGF delivery point). Thus, the gas from ST-CGF cannot be assured to be exported to the NCS 2 pipeline
risks.effect:
- Design change fall between the 2 categories:
1. Keep current configuration and update design conditions . However, the GDU need to be revisited as concerning on package performance and glycol loss when operate at very high pressure (no experience project operate at this pressure). 
Update 11Mar26: Technical Requisition was launch off to Bidders and TBE has been completed with 04 four Bidders/Manufacturers (Jord, FHE/Axens, ISS, PVDT/Ceco) confirmed comply performance in high pressure condition (151 barg opt pressure).
2. Relocate the Gas Dehydration system upstream of the Compression system 
- Further impacts to Process data (material selection, piping class, process pressure & temperature,...), deliverables (drawings, datasheets,...) of all related System, equipment
- Subsequently impact to Project schedule due to the delay in issuance of P&ID, 30/60/90 percent Model review, TR of critical packages,... impacted by the change of Process data
- Implementing the design will exceed the Project budget
risks.mitigationEffect:
1. Official letter to request for change
2. Raise VO for additional SOW
3. Finalize the design with GDU, MRU, and layout of equipment location
11Mar26: Engage closely in process performance review during package Vendor Data review.
4. Re-assess budget for Project execution and EPCIC price
risks.actualActions: Following mitigation plan action
risks.remark:
- CPY official instruction in letter 831 --> firmed Scope of work updated officially
- Budget revised in final EPCIC proposal

risks.title: Anchors mooring under bridges (if using HLB’s anchoring)
risks.description: When utilizing conventional HLB anchoring arrangements, mooring lines and anchors may pass beneath bridges or near existing platforms and structures, which may lead to collision/ clashing / unintended impacts between mooring systems, vessels, and adjacent offshore facilities
risks.cause:
1. Vessel, equipment, or mooring line movement make impact to the bridge/ platform due to inaccurate anchor positioning or handling execution
2. Inadequate anchoring arrangement or clearance analysis
3. Uncontrolled vessel drift or mooring line deviation
4. Limited offshore working space and difficult weather condition
risks.effect:
1. Damage to existing platforms, bridges, vessels, or mooring lines
2. Delay of offshore installation activities
3. Potential impact on surrounding live facilities and operational integrity
risks.mitigationCause:
1. Utilize a suitable anchoring methodology and optimize anchor arrangement
2. Perform detailed anchor path simulation
3. Perform anchor handling activities only under acceptable weather
4. Consider the use of soft mooring lines
5. Consider stringline moor to platform leg (analysis for allowable of limited load)
6. Consider LQM2 installation before the Bridge (CPY advised)
risks.mitigationEffect:
1. Install fenders or structural protection at bridge, insurance coverage, emergency recovery plan
2. Suspend operations and resume only under favorable weather condition
3. Loading capacity of mooring on Jacket legs to be checked by DE for mooring.

4. Select launching window at high tide with adequate tidal margin
5. Require Bidder to provide Launching feasibility report to verify
6. Clearly define and strictly comply with weather and environment limitations
risks.mitigationEffect:

2. Prepare contingency procedures for immediate suspension of launching if clearance limits are approached

2. Increase in jacket weight compared to initial assumptions / FEED data

risks.effect:

2. Structural damage to the jacket during lifting or upending
3. Inability to safely complete jacket upending and offshore installation activities
4. Delay to offshore campaign and associated marine spread standby costs
risks.mitigationCause:
1. Strictly control and monitor final jacket weight 
2. Verify HLB crane capacity at the actual hook height and operating radius
3. Strictly implement the controlled-ballasting procedure
risks.mitigationEffect:

2. Prepare contingency plan, including fenders around HLB to reduce effective lifting radius if needed.
3. Assess feasibility and contingency planning for dual-crane lifting operations
4. Evaluate backup options for a higher-capacity HLB
5. Establish emergency response and recovery procedures

risks.title: Marine Collision & Security Exposure Between Campaigns (Jacket in 2027 and Topside in 2028)
risks.description: After Jacket installation in July 2027 campaign and prior to Topsides installation in April 2028 campaign, the unmanned Jacket and Link Bridge remains exposed offshore for ~9 months, creating risk of vessel collision, structural damage, security breach, or navigation hazard due to inadequate marking, AIS signaling, or marine exclusion enforcement.
risks.cause:
1. Inadequate marine navigation marking (lights, buoys, RACON, AIS AtoN)
2. Failure or power loss of navigation aids
3. Non-compliant passing vessels / fishing boats
4. Extreme weather or poor visibility
5. Absence of active guard vessel enforcement
6. Vandalism or unauthorized boarding
risks.effect:
1. Vessel collision with Jacket
2. Structural damage requiring offshore repair campaign
3. Misalignment affecting Topsides installation tolerances
4. HSE incident (marine casualty, fatalities)
risks.mitigationCause:
1. Install Class-compliant Navigation Aids (IALA compliant) for active vessel awareness
2. Implement AIS AtoN (Automatic Identification System – Aid to Navigation)
3. Install RACON and passive radar reflector systems reflector for radar visibility and vessel detection
4. Recommend CPY to provide Guard vessel (security boat) 
5. Define clear custody, responsibility between offshore campaigns
6. Establish active monitoring by Operations teams from existing facilities
7. Confirm adequacy of CAR (Construction All Risk) insurance coverage during idle period
8. Handover care & custody to CPY once completion (before demob) of installation each Package/ Object
risks.mitigationEffect:
1. Maintain periodic offshore inspection and installation tolerance re-verification plans
2. Activate insurance claim procedures promptly
3. Conduct dimensional re-survey and structural reassessment

risks.title: Escalation of Middle East Geopolitical Conflict Impacting Global Supply Chain & Shipping Routes
risks.description:
Escalation of armed or political conflict involving the USA, Israel, Iran, and regional countries may lead to the closure of the Suez Canal, disrupting Europe–Asia shipping routes.
Vessels would be forced to reroute via the Cape of Good Hope, increasing transit time, freight costs, and potentially affecting the availability and delivery schedule.
risks.cause:
1. Military escalation or retaliatory strikes
2. Sanctions expansion or trade restrictions
3. Increased maritime security threats (missile/drone attacks, vessel seizure)
risks.effect:
1. Congestion at alternative ports
2. Disruption of long-lead equipment delivery
3. SubContractor claims for EOT and cost variation
4. Shipping delays (2-4 weeks depending on rerouting)
5. Increased freight costs
risks.mitigationCause:
1. Continuous geopolitical intelligence monitoring
2. Early engagement with logistics providers on alternative routing
3. Contractual review for sanctions / force majeure clauses
4. Diversify suppliers geographically where feasible
5. Advance procurement of long-lead items
risks.mitigationEffect:
1. Increase schedule buffer for critical deliveries
2. Negotiate flexible Incoterms and delivery windows
3. Secure war risk insurance coverage clarity
4. Maintain contingency budget for freight escalation
5. Prioritize early fabrication and preservation storage where possible
6. Re-evaluate the lead time of packages in Procurement Plan with origins from EU

risks.title: Inadequate Flatness Control for Top of DSF Surface and Topside Can Base PL
risks.description: Failure to achieve required flatness tolerance at the top surface of Deck Support Frame (DSF) and Topside Can Base Plate may result in uneven load transfer during lowering Topsides on DSF, causing excessive local stress, shim stacking, misalignment, or structural damage.
risks.cause:
1. Uneven flatness during fabrication of base plate
2. Welding distortion during DSF fabrication, Topside fabrication
3. Insufficient dimensional control and survey control points
4. Improper sequence of Base plate, Ring installation
5. Yard surface or uneven support during fabrication
risks.effect:
1. Uneven load distribution at mating interface
2. Excessive shim thickness (> allowable limit)
3. Local overstress at support stools
4. Installation delay during Jacking
5. Rework (grinding, pad welding, machining)
6. Risk of structural fatigue
risks.owner: DD Truong/ PT Anh/ NT Anh
risks.mitigationCause:
1. Develop effective sequence for control flatness
2. Dimension control during fabrication and welding
3. Control flatness of Ring plate (on Topside Can base PL) and Top Ring of DSF
risks.mitigationEffect:
1. Prepare shim plate as backup plan
2. Effective Dimension report in details
3. Develop method statement to compensate for out of tolerance flatness
4. Use controlled welding sequence to reduce distortion
5. Ensure uniform ground support under DSF during fabrication

risks.description: The Over-deadweight Jacket barge requires approval permit from the Authorities prior to mobilization the barge (7-8 months). Delays in the Authority approval process may impact the readiness of loadout.

risks.title: Failure of FJC for Riser at late stage under Jacket Fabrication subcontractor (VSP) or Tie-in spool under T&I subcontractor
risks.description: Field Joint Coating (FJC) of the riser located underneath the Jacket may fail to meet quality testing requirements during the final onshore fabrication stage.
risks.cause:
1. Complexity of FJC application, including material instability, high sensitivity to temperature and environmental conditions, and stringent testing.
2. Inadequate material, equipment, qualified personnel, or application procedures for FJC works. 
3. Limited accessibility and difficult working conditions
risks.effect:
1. Delay to the jacket load-out schedule, directly impacting the T&I marine campaign milestone
2. Re-coating or repair works, resulting in additional schedule impact
risks.mitigationCause:
1. Engage the FJC specialist/service provider at an early stage
2. Implement strict QA/QC hold points and inspection for FJC application.
3. Clearly define acceptance criteria, testing methodology, and repair procedures
risks.mitigationEffect:
1. Prepare contingency schedule for potential re-coating and repair works
2. Assess impacts to load-out window and notify T&I subcontractor accordingly
3. Prioritize critical inspection and repair activities to minimize schedule.

risks.title: Jacket Installed out of Tolerance may Impact on Link Bridge Installation
risks.description: The final offshore position, elevation, or verticality of the installed jacket may exceed allowable construction tolerances, potentially affecting the alignment, fit-up, and installation of the link bridge
risks.cause:
1. Inaccuracy or signal failure in marine survey and positioning equipment
2. Human error during offshore positioning, leveling, or installation execution
3. Environmental conditions (wave, current, wind) affecting jacket positioning accuracy
4. Unexpected soil resistance or uneven pile penetration depth during jacket setting or piling operations.
risks.effect:
1. Inability to land and secure the link bridge without structural modifications
2. Additional rework to accommodate dimensional deviations
3. Cost impact and schedule delay to subsequent offshore activities
4. Increased offshore interface complexity and installation risk
risks.mitigationCause:
1. Perform multi-team cross-checking
2. Utilize alternative/ secondary positioning and survey systems as backup
3. Ensure qualified survey personnel and calibrated survey equipment are mobilized for operations
4. Monitor weather conditions and execute installation only within approved operational limits
risks.mitigationEffect:
1. Define allowable tolerance envelope for link bridge installation
2. Upon receipt of the jacket dimensional survey report, assess and implement required onshore bridge modifications if necessary

risks.title: Incorrect Metrology of subsea spool may impact to leak testing
risks.description: Dimensional or alignment errors during the subsea metrology survey for the closing spool (including acoustic or photogrammetry measurements), lead to incorrect fabrication measurements and failed hydrotesting.
risks.cause:
1. Subsea survey equipment malfunction, calibration shift, or physical misalignment of target frames. Unnoticed shifting or settlement of the subsea structures between the metrology survey points.
2. Human error during metrology activities
3. Less experience of divers/ survey personnel/ filed engineers
4. Inadequate verification and validation of survey data
risks.effect:
1. High residual stresses or severe mismatch during offshore spool fit-up
2. Flange misalignment resulting in damaged gaskets, leaks of hydrotesting
3. Schedule impact for re-fabrication, modification, or rework
4. Delay to offshore schedule
risks.mitigationCause:
1. Utilize redundant metrology methods, including acoustic measurement and photogrammetry verification
2. Conduct independent verification of survey data processing
3. Define hold points in subsea spool fabrication ITP tied to metrology approval
4. Deploy qualified and experienced metrology specialists, divers, and field engineers with valid calibrated equipment.
risks.mitigationEffect:
1. Include schedule float for spool re-fabrication in offshore campaign planning
2. Pre-position tooling and materials for contingency re-welding offshore

risks.title: Responsibility Boundary for Umbilical Testing between T&I vs HUC (TUTU to SUTU)
risks.description: The T&I scope covers from SUTU to the Top of Jacket, while the HUC scope covers from the Top of Jacket to TUTU. In the event of a leak occurring within the T&I section during HUC testing (whole sections SUTU to TUTU), responsibility may become disputed.
risks.cause:
1. Unclear scope boundaries between T&I and HUC workscopes
2. Absence of defined handover documentation and testing protocol
risks.effect:
1. Operational stand-by and schedule delays from disputes over which party to perform the testing
2. Integrity risks or damage to the umbilical if left untested during a prolonged handover gap
3. Legal and financial liability issues if a testing failure occurs
risks.mitigationCause:
1. Clarify contractual scope boundaries in T&I and HUC contracts
2. Establish a clear testing responsibility matrix with defined holdpoints
risks.mitigationEffect:
1. Establish a formal handover protocol and custody document
2. Assign a dedicated interface manager for T&I/HUC boundary

risks.title: Improper protection & preservation work negatively affects the quality of the project.
risks.description: Improper protection & preservation work negatively affects the quality of the project.
risks.cause:
1. Preservation work is not carried out according to the plan.
2. Lack of manpower & tools/consumable for protection & preservation work.
3. Preservation work is not performed correctly or in line with the manufacturer's guidelines.
4. The construction work arrangement is not well organized, leading to clashing tasks that affect the quality of preservation.
5. There is a lack of continuous monitoring and inspection of preservation work from the equipment manufacturing stage at the factory through delivery to site, storage, construction, and commissioning
6. Improper material selection and non-compliance with vendor or project coating/preservation requirements.
7. No clear preservation plan for FIM packages.
8. Inexperienced construction personnel.
risks.effect:
1. Additional inspection work is required to check the internal condition of equipment and systems to evaluate how they have been affected.
2. Dismantle equipment and system components to rectify the effects
3. Equipment/material damage results in repair or replacement, that impacts the project cost and schedule
risks.mitigationCause:
1. Develop a proper plan and checklist for Protection and Preservation for all equipment and expedite relative team to follow up.
2. Establish a preservation team with an organizational chart that identifies focal personnel and the workforce responsible for preservation activities across all project phases, including from equipment fabrication at the factory, storage in the warehouse, installation at the site, precom/commissioning.
3. Material/consumable & tools for preservation shall be input in the budget and prepared for readiness.
4. A coordinator shall be assigned to expedite and monitor the preservation work.
5. Define vendor requirements for coated materials, preservation methods, and inspection records in purchase documents and technical specifications.
6. Prepare a specific preservation plan for FIM packages, including packing, storage, transportation, and installation stages.
7. Provide training and lessons-learned workshops for workers, supervisors, and the preservation team to ensure correct execution.
risks.mitigationEffect:
1. Special tool for internal inspection the internal condition of equipment and systems shall be prepared in advance (Borescope equipment)
2. Spare material (Gasket, bolts) and manpower shall be prepared.
3. Sensitive component/equipment/material must be carefully protected and preserved in strict accordance with the manufacturer’s requirements. Spare materials should be considered for procurement.
4. Unpainted surface must be coated or wrapped with denso tape to protect against rust and corrosion.

risks.title: Risk of topside deck deformation during construction
risks.description:
The topside deck structure will be deformed during construction:
- After deck lifting
- After equipment installtion
- After remove temporary support.
- After jacking and install the topside onto the DSF
- Joint/Node assembly OOT
risks.cause:
1. The structural design may not be sufficiently strong, especially at the support locations for large equipment such as GTG, GTC, vessels, MRUs, etc.
2. Not enough temporary support for deck assembly/lifting and under large equipment.
3. Improper control of Welding sequence during Deck Fabrication & Assembly.
4. Lack of Dimension check following the Dimension control Procedure
risks.effect:
1. Rework may be required to rectify deck deformation, resulting in schedule delay and additional cost.
2. Equipment leveling may become out of tolerance. 
3. Additional replacement materials may be required for repair
risks.mitigationCause:
1. DE to re-check the deck structural design calculations and provide reinforcement where required. 
2. CE and Construction to review and enhance temporary supports for deck assembly, deck lifting, and equipment support locations. 
3. Coordinate with QC to establish and control the proper welding sequence for deck fabrication and assembly.
4. Monitor deck leveling and dimensions, provide extra reinforcement throughout the construction stage.
risks.mitigationEffect:
1. Monitor levelling of equipment after installation.
2. Procure spare shim plate for alignment & levelling equipment.
3. Check spare materials from Company or orther project stock.

risks.title: Topside-to-jacket misalignment during offshore installation.
risks.description:
Misalignment at tie-in point during the installation of the topside onto the jacket at offshore:
- Topside to Jacket
- HUC Riser spool & J-tube
- Seawater caisson
risks.cause:
1. Uncontrolled dimensional checks at jacket–topside interface points during fabrication and installation.
2. Jacket structural deformation after offshore installation.
3. Topside structural deformation after Jacking and Loadout.
4. Failure of measuring and survey equipment.
risks.effect:
1. Impact to T&I, HUC, and overall Project Schedule.
2. Rework, repair, and modification works.
3. Impact to Project Cost, including vessel extension.
risks.owner: DD Truong/ PT Anh/DC Nguyen/Ta Van Minh
risks.mitigationCause:
1. Implement a strict QA/QC dimensional control plan at the fabrication yard for interface points.
2. Ensure clear definition of installation tolerances and alignment requirements.
3. Refer to the actual dimensional reports from the Jacket and DSF for assembly interface points between the Topside and Jacket/DSF.
4. Perform final dimensional inspection before topside sail-away..
risks.mitigationEffect:

2. Mobilize additional resources for corrective works if needed.

risks.title: Uncontrol the outstanding work related to equipment package.
risks.description:
Uncontrol the outstanding work related to equipment package after these arrived at site:
- FAT punchlist, outstanding work
- OS&D
risks.cause:
1. No effective tracking system for punch list and outstanding items (no clear register or status updates).
2. Poor coordination between PE, Expeditor, Vendor, CPY, and site team.

2. Prioritize to close out all critical item for precom/commisioning.
3. Escalate critical delays early to management.
4. Deploy additional resources (manpower / expediting team) where delays are critical.

risks.title: The E&I construction activities are experiencing schedule delays
risks.description: For recent projects, E&I construction activities have frequently experienced schedule delays, as observed in projects such as Baltica2 and LDV.

risks.mitigationEffect:
1. Arrange sufficient supervision resources to monitor the progress of E&I works, assess potential schedule delay risks, and prepare timely manpower supplement plans to ensure recovery and alignment with the project schedule.

risks.title: Barge Leakage potential Impact on Loadout Laytime and Project Schedule
risks.description: Leakage of the HTV/barge may occur before or during mobilization to the fabrication yard due to deterioration of the bulkhead structure and/or internal ballast system, may affect the barge’s integrity, stability, and readiness for loadout and offshore T&I activities
risks.cause:
1. Inadequate pre-mobilization inspection and condition assessment of the barge
2. Poor condition or deterioration of the bulkhead structure and/or internal ballast system
3. Aging barge condition and insufficient maintenance
risks.effect:
1. Loss of stability or operational integrity
2. Impact on laytime duration and offshore execution schedule

risks.title: Risk of clashing, hitting during removal Bouyancy Tanks (BTs)
risks.description: Potential collision or unintended impact between buoyancy tank and adjacent structures during lifting
risks.cause:
1. Immature or insufficiently verified removal design and execution sequence
2. Large size and weight of buoyancy tanks, resulting in limited maneuverability
3. Limited lifting capacity of the HLB
4. Strong sea current, underwater motion, or unfavorable environmental conditions
risks.effect:
1. Damage to jacket members or adjacent subsea structures during buoyancy tank removal
2. Personnel injury or offshore safety incidents
3. Delay to offshore installation and overall schedule
risks.mitigationCause:
1. Design buoyancy tank removal sequences with adequate lifting clearance and operational tolerance, ROV monitoring, installation aids.
2. Monitor sea current and environmental conditions and execute removal activities only within approved weather and sea-state limits
3. 3D model/simulation should be checked by OIC during engineering onshore
risks.mitigationEffect:
1. Jacket protection with bumpers, deploy divers/ROV to intervene impact
2. Perform Engineering analysis and structural inspection immediately following any suspected impact, with repair plans prepared
3. Suspend operations and resume only under favorable weather condition

1. Ballast pumps inefficiency, malfunction, or failure during operation.

2. Ensure all ballast control equipment and instruments are calibrated and functional and to be trial fit/tested of T&I equipment at yard

2. Continuously monitor hook load, center of gravity (CoG) shift, jacket inclination to adjust accordingly.
3. Define operational stop-work criteria and emergency recovery actions in the event of instability or overload
